classification.difficultyReason: Convert each supplied angle to exact unit-circle coordinates using reference angles and quadrant signs, including using the diagram to select the negative y-coordinate for S.

content.prompt: The points $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ are on the unit circle $x^2+y^2=1$. $A$ has coordinates $(1,0)$ and $O$ is the origin. Find the exact coordinates of these points if

spec.description: Unit circle, positive axis arrows, four exterior point labels, A, source scale labels and four radii. P and R are opposite. The origin is defined in the stem; its drawn O label is omitted under the house graph rule. No shading.
spec.mathematics: P at 60 degrees, Q at 120 degrees, R at 240 degrees, S in quadrant IV with a 30-degree reference angle; exact angles come from the page-14 conditions.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied point positions and labels; no coordinate answers or extra angle labels.

answer.worked:
The diagram places $S$ in quadrant IV, so its $y$-coordinate is negative.
$$\begin{align*}S&=(\cos30^\circ,-\sin30^\circ)\\S&=\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2},-\frac12\right)\end{align*}$$
